heading: Voice AI in the Drive-Thru: FAQ

questions.q: What is voice AI ordering in a drive-thru?
questions.a: Voice AI ordering uses natural language processing to take a guest's order at the speaker box, the way a trained team member would. It understands what the guest says, confirms the order and suggests add-ons. Providers like Presto and SoundHound already run it at brands such as Checkers and Del Taco.

questions.q: Is voice AI more accurate than human order takers?
questions.a: Voice AI is starting to outperform human staff on accuracy, speed and upsell consistency in many deployments. It doesn't get tired during a rush, and it handles different languages and accents. Your team still matters for anything that falls outside a standard order.

questions.q: Will voice AI replace drive-thru staff?
questions.a: The model that works best blends the two. AI handles fast, common orders, menu recommendations and promotions, while your team handles custom requests, complaints and service recovery. That frees people to spend their time on the moments that build loyalty.

questions.q: How does drive-thru voice AI personalize suggestions?
questions.a: Voice AI learns from huge numbers of interactions, such as which items pair well, which promos work at different times of day and when guests tend to skip upsells. It uses that to adjust its scripts and suggestions in real time. For example, it might skip offering coffee with an iced drink in the afternoon but suggest it in the morning.

questions.q: Where else will restaurants use voice ordering?
questions.a: Voice is expanding beyond the speaker box into app reordering, hands-free in-car ordering, voice-based loyalty redemption and conversational kiosks in stores. As it does, every guest touchpoint will need to handle a natural conversation. Brands that get there early can offer a faster and more personal experience.
